title: Coffman Conditions for Deadlock
statement: Which of the following is NOT one of the four necessary Coffman conditions required for a deadlock to occur?
explanation: The four Coffman conditions for deadlock are: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption (resources cannot be forcibly taken away), and Circular Wait. 'Preemption Allowed' prevents deadlock.

title: Thrashing in Operating Systems
statement: What causes 'Thrashing' in a virtual memory operating system?

options.text: CPU spending more time swapping pages between RAM and disk than executing user instructions
High CPU utilization with zero disk I/O
Too much free RAM causing TLB misses

explanation: Thrashing occurs when the total working sets of active processes exceed available physical memory, forcing the OS into continuous page faulting and page swapping (I/O) at the expense of CPU execution.

title: Mutex vs Counting Semaphore
statement: What is the key functional distinction between a Binary Semaphore (Mutex) and a Counting Semaphore?

options.text: Mutex includes ownership (only the locking thread can unlock), whereas Counting Semaphore coordinates access to N resource instances and can be signaled by any thread
Counting Semaphore can only take values 0 and 1
Mutex uses busy-waiting while Counting Semaphore never blocks
Counting Semaphore cannot be used in multi-threaded programs

explanation: A Mutex provides exclusive mutual exclusion with strict thread ownership (the thread that acquires the lock must release it). A counting semaphore maintains an integer counter representing available shared resources and can be signaled by producer/consumer threads.

title: Starvation in Shortest Job First (SJF) Scheduling
statement: Which scheduling algorithm is susceptible to process starvation when a continuous stream of short processes arrives?

options.text: Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF / SJF Preemptive)

explanation: In SJF / SRTF, long CPU-bound processes can starve indefinitely if new short processes keep arriving. Round Robin prevents starvation using time slicing.
